brief.headline: Samsung-SK Hynix: KOSPI Concentration Hits 50.7% as DRAM Doubles, HBM4 Converges, Volatility Exceeds Iran War Levels
brief.summary: <cite index="42-1,42-23">Samsung Electronics and SK hynix combined market cap hit 50.7% of the KOSPI as of May 29, surpassing half the index for the first time.</cite> <cite index="38-17,40-1">On June 5, Samsung fell 6.4% and SK Hynix dropped 9.92% amid Broadcom guidance disappointment, with leveraged ETFs down 20%.</cite> <cite index="12-1,16-1">DRAM contract prices surged 90-95% QoQ in Q1 2026, with NAND up 55-60%, driven by hyperscaler AI demand and HBM capacity reallocation.</cite> <cite index="19-6,21-9">Four hyperscalers plan $725B capex in 2026, up 77% YoY, with 2027 estimates above $1T.</cite> <cite index="9-2,9-13">Both companies delivered paid HBM4 final samples to Nvidia; Q1 2026 volume and pricing contracts expected, with HBM3E prices up ~20% and supply tight through 2026.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="1-11,1-17">SK Hynix maintains 62% HBM shipment share (Q2 2025) and is expected to capture ~70% of HBM4 for Nvidia's Rubin platform in 2026, having secured world's first mass production system in September.</cite> <cite index="3-6,3-8">Samsung started HBM4 mass production at Pyeongtaek in February 2026, targeting Nvidia's Vera Rubin (H2 2026) and Google TPU supply, with better performance via 10nm-class vs SK's 12nm base die.</cite> <cite index="9-9,9-18">Samsung plans 50% HBM capacity expansion to 250k wafers/month by end-2026 (up from 170k); SK Hynix's M15X fab started 1b DRAM for HBM4 four months early in February, ramping to 10k wafers/month initially.</cite> Relative call: Neutral with edge to SK Hynix on Nvidia Rubin lock-in and lead-time, but Samsung catching up on qualification (passed Broadcom tests) and capacity delta is material. <cite index="43-8">Samsung customers stated 'Samsung is back' on HBM4, though SK held 53% HBM market share Q3 2025 vs Samsung's 35%.</cite> Watch Q1 pricing finalization for allocation clarity.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="11-2,11-7,11-8">Q2 2026 conventional DRAM contract prices forecast +58-63% QoQ, NAND +70-75% QoQ, following Q1's record 90-95% DRAM jump.</cite> <cite index="13-5,13-6,13-7">Samsung and SK Hynix (70% of global DRAM) signaled no aggressive capacity expansion, prioritizing profitability; memory price rally projected past 2028.</cite> <cite index="13-24,13-25">HBM crowds out commodity DRAM at 3-to-1 conversion ratio per Micron, compressing general-purpose supply.</cite> <cite index="14-7,14-8,14-16">PC DRAM contract prices grew significantly in Q2, upward trend projected into Q3-Q4, though momentum slowed as high costs weakened PC sales.</cite> Structural tightness through 2H26.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="1-7,1-9,4-1,4-6">HBM3E expected to remain flagship product in 2026, accounting for ~66-67% of total HBM output, with HBM4 ramping gradually.</cite> <cite index="6-2,6-4,6-5">Samsung and SK Hynix plan ~20% HBM3E price hike for 2026 as supply lags demand; H200 (6 HBM3E stacks) approval for China exports added unexpected volume, with Nvidia planning 5k-10k modules (40k-80k chips).</cite> <cite index="6-8,6-10">Google TPU v7 and Amazon Trainium shipments begin 2026, with Google using 8 HBM3E stacks/chip, Amazon 4 stacks; HBM content up 20-30% per accelerator.</cite> <cite index="4-11,4-14">Nvidia exploring 16-layer HBM for Q4 2026 delivery (likely HBM4E), with performance evaluation expected before Q3.</cite> <cite index="31-2,31-6">TSMC's CoWoS-L and CoWoS-S fully booked through 2026 driven by Nvidia, Google, Amazon, MediaTek orders; HBM stacks rising from 6 to 8.</cite> <cite index="3-16">HBM production capacity for both Samsung and SK Hynix sold out for next year.</cite>

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix combine for 50.7% of KOSPI; June volatility (3.9% daily avg) exceeds Iran war levels (3.7%)
news_pulse.implication: Extreme concentration risk: any HBM/DRAM headline moves entire Korean equity complex. Leveraged ETF flows amplifying swings.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix -9.92%, Samsung -6.4% on June 5; leveraged ETFs down 20%, hit all-time lows since launch
news_pulse.implication: Broadcom guidance miss triggered panic selloff. Retail trapped in leveraged products; negative compounding in play. Both names oversold short-term.

news_pulse.headline: Q1 2026 DRAM contract prices +90-95% QoQ (revised from 55-60%); NAND +55-60% (from 33-38%)
news_pulse.implication: Memory margins at cycle highs. Server DRAM >60% QoQ, LPDDR ~90% QoQ gains. CSPs/OEMs locked in allocation wars through 2H26.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix delivered paid HBM4 final samples to Nvidia; Q1 2026 volume/pricing contracts pending
news_pulse.implication: Final qualification underway. Nvidia Rubin (H2 2026) allocation split determines 2027 share gains. Both vendors passed SiP tests.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler capex $725B in 2026 (up 77% YoY); Goldman sees $5.3T cumulative 2025-2030 for top 4
news_pulse.implication: AI capex accelerating into 2027 ($1T+). Nvidia GPU + HBM demand structurally bid. Memory vendors pricing power sustained 2+ years.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS-L/S fully booked; capacity to hit 130k wafers/month by end-2026 (up from 35k in late 2024)
news_pulse.implication: Advanced packaging bottleneck easing but Nvidia locks 60%+ allocation. HBM attach rate rising (8-12 stacks per GPU). 16-layer HBM4E pulls forward generational shift.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung HBM4 started mass production February 2026 at Pyeongtaek; SK M15X fab four months early, 10k wafers/month
news_pulse.implication: Both vendors racing to lock Rubin supply. Samsung using 10nm base die (vs SK 12nm) claims 11.7Gbps speeds. Capacity ramp critical for 2H26 revenue.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix plan ~20% HBM3E price hike 2026; supply tight as HBM4 ramp prioritized
news_pulse.implication: H200 China exports + Google TPU v7 + Amazon Trainium demand exceed supply. HBM3E mix 45% of revenue in 2026 vs HBM4 55% from Q3 onward.

brief.derivatives_signal: Implied vol spike post-June 5 selloff; KOSPI 200 futures term structure inverted. Single-stock leveraged ETF capitulation suggests short-term oversold, but concentration (>50% index weight) makes delta-hedging expensive. Watch June 9-13 window for Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Korea visit—likely catalyst for snap-back rally if HBM allocation commentary surfaces. Near-term skew elevated; consider ATM call spreads on 2-week tenor if stabilization holds.
watch_for_next_3h: Nvidia Rubin (H2 2026) HBM4 allocation leaks—any vendor-specific commentary moves both stocks 5%+
Q2 2026 DRAM/NAND contract pricing guidance updates from TrendForce (due mid-June)—current forecast +58-63% DRAM, +70-75% NAND
SK Hynix M15X ramp progress (1b DRAM for HBM4)—10k wafers/month baseline vs target multi-fold scale by end-2026
Samsung HBM4 Broadcom test results follow-up after passing initial SiP validation—critical for non-Nvidia revenue diversification
KOSPI circuit breaker risk if concentration >51% and another Mag7 disappointment hits—monitor retail leveraged ETF liquidation flows
